daily.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
daily.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

daily.title: Pope Leo vs. Javier Milei: How political is the pope?
daily.summary: Pope Leo XIV's tour of South America has drawn huge crowds — and a measure of political controversy. Perceived criticism of Argentina's leader, and earlier rebukes of Donald Trump, offer a glimpse into papacy politics.

daily.title: Japan watches for signs of change in Trump's foreign policy priorities
daily.summary: Tokyo fears the drubbing US President Donald Trump suffered in last week's midterm elections may push him to pursue a diplomatic quick win at the expense of Washington's allies in the Indo-Pacific.

daily.title: Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
daily.summary: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

daily.title: India: Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' released
daily.summary: The book goes through the Italian-born matriarch's journey with one of India's most politically influential families. It has already garnered political controversy, with the ruling BJP accusing her of "whitewashing."

daily.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
daily.summary: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

daily.title: Spain: Police officer killed in Oviedo after neighborhood dispute escalates with explosion
daily.summary: After security services responded to a shooting, a bomb found in a backpack nearby detonated before it could be defused.

daily.title: Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
daily.summary: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

daily.title: DR Congo: 66 soldiers sentenced to death for 'cowardice' in conflict with FRN rebels
daily.summary: Dozens of defendants were put on trial over accusations that they abandoned their posts and refused to follow direct orders.

daily.title: Germany news: President candidate Aigner to meet parties in Bundestag
daily.summary: The presidential candidate put forward by the conservative bloc has said she won't meet with the far-right AfD. Meanwhile, Chancellor Merz is set to host Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar. DW has more.

daily.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
daily.summary: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

daily.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
daily.summary: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

daily.title: US, Russia and Ukraine start talks in Abu Dhabi
daily.summary: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US are getting underway in the United Arab Emirates. It is the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

daily.title: India news: New Delhi ready to mediate Black Sea food corridors, says Ukraine's Zelenskyy
daily.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he discussed establishing "food corridors" in the Black Sea in a phone call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

daily.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
daily.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

daily.title: Australia to introduce mandatory AI safeguards
daily.summary: The Australian government's decision to establish an AI safety regulator comes after an OpenAI agent accessed a government medical statistics portal without authorization.

daily.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
daily.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

daily.title: Nvidia shareholders sue Jensen Huang over alleged spy ties
daily.summary: Nvidia shareholders have sued the chipmaker and its CEO, Jensen Huang, over his alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy. The case adds to scrutiny over whether sensitive information at the AI giant was compromised.

daily.title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
daily.summary: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

daily.title: Skydance replaces James Gunn and Peter Safran as DC Studios chiefs following Warner Bros. takeover
daily.summary: In another major shake-up for the DC Studios, Skydance is replacing Hollywood director James Gunn and producer Peter Safran with a former Marvel executive.

daily.title: Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
daily.summary: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.

daily.title: Ice hockey: Norway says it's been kicked out of World Juniors in favor of Russia
daily.summary: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

weekly.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
weekly.summary: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

weekly.title: Germany: CDU names Ilse Aigner as candidate for president
weekly.summary: The steering committtee of the CDU have announced Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as presidential candidate. This gives her a good chance of becoming the first woman to occupy the role.

weekly.title: EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
weekly.summary: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

weekly.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
weekly.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

weekly.title: Who is Ilse Aigner, leading candidate for Germany's next president?
weekly.summary: She would be the first female president and the first Christian Social Union politician to hold Germany's highest office. Ilse Aigner is the favored candidate for the Federal Convention vote on January 30.

weekly.title: Germany news: Germany marks fateful date of November 9
weekly.summary: Germany is commemorating the Nazi-led November pogroms 88 years ago. Events are also being held to mark the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. DW has more.

weekly.title: Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
weekly.summary: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

weekly.title: Germany: Chancellor Merz to nominate Aigner for president
weekly.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.

weekly.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
weekly.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

weekly.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
weekly.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

weekly.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
weekly.summary: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

weekly.title: Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
weekly.summary: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

weekly.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
weekly.summary: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

weekly.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
weekly.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Russia hits Kyiv with airstrikes ahead of trilateral talks
weekly.summary: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to "push" Ukraine "into a blackout" ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

weekly.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
weekly.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

weekly.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
weekly.summary: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

weekly.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
weekly.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

weekly.title: Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
weekly.summary: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

weekly.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
weekly.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

weekly.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
weekly.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

weekly.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
weekly.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

weekly.title: Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins postelection cleanup
weekly.summary: The landslide victory of the Student List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

weekly.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
weekly.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?

weekly.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
weekly.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

weekly.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
weekly.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

weekly.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
weekly.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

weekly.title: Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
weekly.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

weekly.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
weekly.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

weekly.title: 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
weekly.summary: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

weekly.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
weekly.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

weekly.title: Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
weekly.summary: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

weekly.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
weekly.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

weekly.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
weekly.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

weekly.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
weekly.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

weekly.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
weekly.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

weekly.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
weekly.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

weekly.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
weekly.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
